analysis.title: Building resilience for 2027 (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: UBS launched its Year Ahead 2027 outlook, 'Sustaining resilience'. It expects global growth near trend, rising corporate earnings, continued AI infrastructure investment, and modestly lower bond yields later in 2027 as inflation eases.

UBS downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral, citing elevated expectations, index concentration and uncertainty around the AI investment cycle. It sees a more balanced risk-reward after a multi-year bull run.
Cross-asset preference order: bonds and commodities have the most favorable risk-reward, then equities, with cash the least preferred asset class.

Risk scenarios: sticky inflation, elevated government debt and geopolitical risks could push bond yields higher and equities lower. A second scenario is execution and monetization risk undermining confidence in AI returns across the value chain.

UBS expects global AI-related investment to rise from USD 1.0 trillion in 2026 to USD 1.5 trillion in 2028. Cumulative US technology investment could approach USD 5.0 trillion by then, and revenues probably need to reach at least USD 1.5 trillion by 2030 for an adequate return.

AI return threats named: competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models. External financing is becoming harder, and concentration, regulatory and company-specific risks could raise volatility.

The top 10 S&P 500 firms, most exposed to AI, are 39% of the index. UBS says the market may start applying a lower multiple to future earnings to reflect rising risks, including stickier inflation, higher Fed policy rates and higher bond yields.

Equity positioning: refocus and diversify away from concentrated technology exposure. The Eurozone is the preferred equity market, with 2027 earnings growth forecast at 15%, comparable to the S&P 500 but from a lower valuation and with broader earnings drivers.

Sector and structure preferences: industrials and health care favored, and US equal-weight strategies suggested to reduce tech concentration. The equal-weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the cap-weighted index by about 7 percentage points since the start of June.

Bonds: elevated starting yields give income and a cushion against rising rates. The best fixed income return opportunity is in emerging market and high yield bonds. US high yield is 60% BB, with expected defaults around 2% and 3% of the universe maturing within a year.
UBS favors intermediate average duration, generally maturities of about two to 10 years, with shorter-dated bonds preferred in more growth-sensitive credit segments.
Gold upgraded to Attractive. Structural demand and an eventual easing in real yields should support a recovery toward USD 5,000 an ounce by December 2027.
Oil should stay supported in the first half of 2027. Copper is the preferred industrial metal on demand from electrification, power networks, data centers and AI infrastructure.

Currencies and alternatives: sterling is the preferred G10 carry opportunity, and select EM currencies may benefit from high yields and contained volatility. Favored alternatives are dispersion-focused hedge fund strategies, operationally focused private equity and secondaries, and infrastructure with visible cash flows.

Central message: do not retreat from markets, but take risk more deliberately by putting excess cash to work, addressing concentration, rebalancing toward fixed income and adding differentiated return drivers.
